title: Looking for clever, nuanced satires about relationships like Force Majeure?

commenti.body: Phantom Thread is the only one that comes to mind, but that one is not very satirical besides perhaps a few moments (the bread buttering scene). Still, it's a similar nuanced slow burn drama about a relationship through it's ups and downs.

I was going to suggest The Square but then looked it up on Letterboxed and found out it was by the same director as Force Majeure, Ruben Ostlund. 

Maybe Paul Thomas Anderson captures this type of quality? Not satire, but your description reminded me of Punch Drunk Love and Magnolia. 

Also kind of reminded me of Christopher Guest movies.

Does anybody know of a film in which women take such a self-critical and self-aware look at themselves with regard to their own less appealing tendencies in relationships? I would be interested to know if such a thing exists.

I think The Lobster fits this probably. Other ones I'm less convinced of, but still think are worth mentioning are Le Bonheur and Carnal knowledge. These are more skewed towards the tragedy of the male perspective, opposed to focusing on both partners of the relationship. I thought all three were hilarious though.
Oh? You were laughing at the “hilarious” end of Carnal Knowledge?

- 8 1/2
- The Worst Person in the World
- Alle Anderen
- Tuesday After Christmas
- Late Marriage
- Claire’s Knee
- Holiday
- In the Company of Men
- Listen Up Philip
- Golden Exits
- Before Midnight
- Blindspotting
- Drinking Buddies

The Lobster fits perfectly,  maybe less of a mature and detailed exploration of the topic but still a great film and is definitely what I'm looking for. I haven't seen the other two but look forward to it!

Definitely a good pick for what I'm looking for. And "satire" in my title can practically be ignored, as I've sat with this post I realize satire isn't exactly the point, more just the exploration of behaviors with a sense of humor.

What I find hilarious is not necessarily the ending, which is a shocking tragedy. But more the ineptitude of the two main characters to view women as human beings, and how to film fully commits to their worldview. They think they possess the Carnal Knowledge to conquer women, but the entire film is about them eventually knowing very little. 

  
Hilarious isn’t the first word I would use to describe the film, but I did find the film funny and was laughing throughout. But with how relevant it is today, 50 years later, a bitter laugh that is.
